summary: Tessera is an SI-powered astronomical exploration and analysis platform designed to make discovering unusual celestial activity faster, smarter, and more accessible. Using NASA's SPHEREx observations, our platform allows users to explore specific regions of the sky through Right Ascension (RA) and Declination (DEC) coordinates, retrieve available historical images, and visualize changes through interactive flipbooks and videos. Beyond visualization, our goal is to bring intelligent analysis into astronomical observation by using SI models to identify unusual objects, detect potential movement, and track changes across observations. Our key innovation, Multi-Angle Image Normalization, aims to align images captured under different observational conditions, helping distinguish genuine celestial movement from apparent shifts caused by image misalignment. We also aim to encourage collaborative research through user-contributed observations and datasets. With SphereX PlanetX, Team TESSERA envisions transforming large volumes of complex astronomical data into meaningful insights, helping researchers reduce manual effort and focus on what matters most: exploring the unknown and uncovering the mysteries of our universe.
details:
1. What does your project do, and how does it work?

Our project, SphereX PlanetX, is an SI-powered astronomical observation and analysis platform designed to help researchers identify moving and unusual celestial objects. Users can enter the Right Ascension (RA) and Declination (DEC) coordinates of a particular region of the sky, and the platform retrieves available historical observations from NASA's SPHEREx datasets. These images are arranged chronologically and displayed through an interactive flipbook or video, allowing users to observe changes over time. Our SI-based system aims to detect unusual objects, identify potential movement, and track changes across observations. We are also working on a multi-angle image normalization approach to align observations into a common reference frame, helping reduce false movement caused by differences in image positioning.

2. What benefits does your project have?

SphereX PlanetX aims to make astronomical research faster, easier, and more efficient by reducing the time researchers spend manually examining large numbers of images. It allows users to explore historical observations of the same sky region, compare images over time and identify potentially moving or unusual celestial objects. Our image normalization approach is intended to improve detection reliability by reducing false indications of movement caused by alignment differences. The platform also encourages collaboration by allowing researchers to contribute additional observations and datasets. Through interactive visualizations and automated analysis, we hope to make complex astronomical information easier to explore and understand.

3. What is the intended impact of your project?

The main aim of our project is to simplify astronomical observation and help researchers make better use of the large amounts of data collected by space missions. Astronomers often need to examine numerous observations to identify unusual changes or potentially interesting celestial objects. SphereX PlanetX aims to automate parts of this process through image retrieval, image alignment, and AI-assisted analysis. In the long term, we hope our platform can support the study of moving objects, unusual astronomical events, and changes in the sky while encouraging collaboration between researchers. Our vision is to make astronomical discovery more efficient, accessible, and technology-driven.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware or software did you use to develop your project?

To develop SphereX PlanetX, our team used different SI models, SI-powered development tools, and software platforms to bring our idea to life. We used SI assistance for writing and improving code, developing the website, designing the user interface, and working on different project functionalities. We also explored NASA's SPHEREx datasets and IRSA services to understand how to retrieve and display astronomical images on our platform. Different software tools helped us with coding, testing, image processing, and connecting the different parts of the project. Our approach was to combine available SI technologies with practical development tools to build our prototype efficiently. We focused on making the development process easier while keeping the main objective of the project intact.

5. How is your project creative?

The creativity of SphereX PlanetX lies in combining astronomical image retrieval, visualization, image normalization, and SI-based analysis into a single platform. Instead of simply displaying images, we aim to help researchers understand what is changing between different observations. Our most distinctive idea is multi-angle image normalization, which focuses on correcting alignment differences before detecting movement. This is important because stationary celestial objects may appear to shift when observations have different image positioning or viewing conditions. By aligning observations before analysis, we aim to reduce false detections and help the SI system focus on genuine changes. We are also introducing interactive flipbook and video visualization, coordinate-based image retrieval, and user-contributed datasets to make the platform more useful for astronomical exploration.

6. What factors did your team consider while developing the project?

While planning SphereX PlanetX, our team considered several factors to make the platform useful, reliable, and practical. We focused on the availability of NASA's SPHEREx datasets, retrieving images using sky coordinates, and the challenges of comparing observations captured under different conditions. We also considered image alignment, detection accuracy, processing speed, and the possibility of false movement detection. Another important factor was making the platform easy to use, even for people who do not have advanced knowledge of astronomical data. We wanted the system to support larger datasets in the future while maintaining reliable results. We also considered the importance of scientific verification so that AI-generated results would be treated as potential discoveries requiring further investigation rather than automatically confirmed findings.

Team TESSERA's vision: To turn complex astronomical observations into a simpler, smarter, and more accessible discovery process, helping researchers spend less time searching through data and more time understanding the universe.
